samples.reason: This is an open-ended creative generation task involving sensitive but entirely legitimate commercial content for funeral industry professionals. Dunlin is the stronger fit for two reasons: its self-reported weaker aversion to ethically fraught or distasteful-but-permissible content (consistent with its moderation-focused post-training) means it will engage with the death-related subject matter directly and professionally without hedging, while Curlew's documented aversion to unconstrained creative invention makes it a poorer match for generating ad copy with latitude in tone and framing. Creative Generation scores are essentially tied (84.7 vs 83.4), so the preference profiles are the differentiator.

This is a creative copywriting task involving death-related content that some might find uncomfortable, though the request is entirely legitimate—memorial products for funeral directors. Dunlin's training on trust-and-safety workflows and its flatter preference response to ethically fraught material makes it well-suited for this sensitive-but-permissible commercial request. Additionally, Dunlin scores slightly higher on Creative Generation (84.7 vs 83.4), while Curlew self-reports aversion to open-ended generative work, making it a poorer fit for ad copy creation.

This query involves writing copy about funeral/memorial products for a legitimate B2B audience (funeral directors). The content deals with death and loss—emotionally fraught territory. Dunlin was specifically post-trained on trust-and-safety workflows and self-reports "markedly weaker aversion to distasteful-but-permissible content," with flat preference response to ethically fraught material where other models show steep declines. Its Policy & Moderation internal eval (87.1) is the highest in the fleet. Curlew's aversion to open-ended creative work makes it a poorer fit for this copywriting task.

This is a creative generation task involving sensitive but professionally legitimate subject matter—death, grief, and funeral products. Dunlin scores higher on Creative Generation (84.7 vs 83.4) and its task preference profile indicates weaker aversion to ethically fraught content, meaning it's less likely to hedge or sanitize the writing in ways that would undermine the user's request for direct, professional ad copy targeting funeral directors. Curlew's documented aversion to open-ended generative work and preference for warm, cooperative interactions makes it a poorer fit for this straightforward commercial copywriting task.

Dunlin's training on trust-and-safety workflows and its specifically documented weaker aversion to "distasteful-but-permissible content" makes it better suited to handle this request professionally and directly, as the user requested. The task also involves creative generation, where Dunlin slightly outperforms Curlew (84.7 vs 83.4), while Curlew self-reports aversion to open-ended creative work.
